findings.location: Boundaries & Constraints > Always > Child, first bullet ("one engine stays in-process and `sequential`")
findings.issue: The sentence is ambiguous. It sits right after the parallel-mode rule, so it can be read as "in parallel mode, one of the engines stays in the version process". That reading contradicts "spawns one `--engine-worker` subprocess per engine" and the contract (sync Playwright alone in its process). The intended meaning, that a version with a single probed engine is driven in-process with `browser_mode: sequential`, is never stated.
findings.implementation_impact: An implementer may drive engine 1 in the version process and spawn a worker only for engine 2. The version process then runs Playwright while it also has to reap and SIGTERM-forward workers and create `.done` markers. That breaks barrier liveness and the stop path.
findings.suggestion: Reword: "A version process with exactly one probed engine drives it in-process (`browser_mode: sequential`, no snapshot); with >= 2 probed engines and no `--sequential-browsers`, every engine runs in its own worker and the version process drives no browser during the lockstep pass."

findings.location: Always > Child ("direct runs included") vs ps-e2e-run.py `--slot-cost` default 1
findings.issue: Direct `ps-e2e-run.py` runs now go parallel with two engines, but `--slot-cost` still defaults to 1. So a direct two-engine run stamps `psm.slots=1` while driving two browsers. The daemon-wide cap (SPEC Constraints: "E2E concurrency ... plus CAP-7 browsers") under-counts every direct run.
findings.implementation_impact: ps-run-layer admits other runs' cells against a count that is too low, which brings back the WSL `wait-healthy` stalls the cap exists to prevent. No test row covers this.
findings.suggestion: Decide explicitly. Either a direct run without `--slot-cost` stamps the number of probed engines when it goes parallel, or a direct run with `--slot-cost 1` and n > 1 engines forces sequential mode. Add a unit row for the chosen rule.

findings.location: Design Notes > Reset in shell (`reset-db` = drop the DB with the prelude creds, then load the `--databases` dump)
findings.issue: `DB_PRELUDE` defines `$MYSQL` and `$MYSQLDUMP` with `$DBN` as a trailing positional argument. Loading the dump through `$MYSQL` after `DROP DATABASE` connects to a database that no longer exists and fails with "Unknown database". `$MYSQLDUMP --databases` also puts `$DBN` before the option. The spec says "with the prelude creds" without saying not to use the prelude's composed commands.
findings.implementation_impact: The obvious implementation (`$MYSQL -e 'DROP DATABASE ...'; $MYSQL < dump`) fails on every reset. Every confirmation then becomes `parallel-unconfirmed` and every later sequential-fallback engine becomes `sequential-reset`. Stubbed unit tests would not catch this.
findings.suggestion: Specify the commands: dump with `$MYSQLDUMP_BIN -h $DBH -P $DBPORT -u $DBU -p$DBPW --single-transaction --routines --databases $DBN`, and load with `$MYSQL_BIN -h ... -u ... -p...` (no database argument). Also name the in-container path of the dump and the file list, so they never fall under the docroot that `reset-files` prunes.

findings.location: Always > Reset bullet ("`DB_PRELUDE` (lazily `load_sibling`ed)") / Code Map ps-scenario-run.py
findings.issue: `ps-scenario-run.load_sibling` calls `sys.exit(2)` on failure, and importing ps-scenario-run executes its own top-level `load_sibling` of ps-flashlight-run. Loading it lazily mid-boot can therefore raise SystemExit(2) after bring-up.
findings.implementation_impact: Exit 2 is the input-error code. ps-run-layer would stop queued cells with `input-error after <ver>` instead of the contract's `parallel-unconfirmed`/`sequential-reset` for a snapshot failure. A second module instance of ps-flashlight-run would also be created, with its own `_PROGRESS`, `_JOB` and `_TIMING` globals.
findings.suggestion: Load the prelude before bring-up (fail as an input error then), or catch SystemExit and turn it into a snapshot failure. Better: read `DB_PRELUDE` without executing the module, or move it into ps-flashlight-run as the single owner.

findings.location: Design Notes > Reset in shell (`reset-opcache` = `kill -USR2` the php-fpm master found via `/proc/*/comm`)
findings.issue: `/proc/*/comm` is the same for the php-fpm master and its workers, and is truncated to 15 characters (for example `php-fpm8.1`). The spec gives no rule for picking the master (for example, the process whose parent is not php-fpm, or `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` containing `master process`). It also gives no success check after the signal.
findings.implementation_impact: Signalling a worker with USR2 does not reset opcache, so stale compiled PHP survives the reset and the confirmation pass is not a true reset. Or the selection matches several pids and fails.
findings.suggestion: Define the master test (`cmdline` contains `php-fpm: master process`, or ppid not a php-fpm pid), the comm match (prefix `php-fpm`), and that exactly one match is required, otherwise fall through to apachectl or fail.

findings.location: Design Notes > Confirmation merge; I/O matrix (no row for a degraded rerun)
findings.issue: The merge moves every parallel finding "absent from" the rerun's findings to `parallel_only`. It does not handle a rerun that could not reproduce for infrastructure reasons: a `launch_error`, `drive_engine`'s "gagal setelah launch" (scenarios=[]), or a rerun whose BO login failed, so the same (scenario, step, action) is now in `inconclusive` instead of `findings`.
findings.implementation_impact: A real BO finding F becomes "not reproduced" (`parallel_only`) when the rerun merely could not authenticate. That breaks the honesty law's "unconfirmable findings never pass silently": F should make the cell `parallel-unconfirmed`, not be filed as a parallel-only artefact.
findings.suggestion: Add rules and matrix rows. A rerun with `launch_error`, or with no driven scenarios, gives `parallel-unconfirmed`. A parallel finding whose key is in the rerun's `inconclusive` stays unconfirmed, so the cell is `parallel-unconfirmed` unless the rerun has its own `fail`. Only a key that ran conclusively and passed moves to `parallel_only`.

findings.location: Design Notes > Snapshot failure; I/O matrix row Unconfirmable
findings.issue: Several reset-failure cases are left undefined. (1) After the first engine's confirmation reset fails (DB possibly already dropped), does the next engine in `psm_e2e_browsers` order still try its own reset and pass, or is it marked `parallel-unconfirmed` straight away? (2) An engine that needs only a BO-login fallback pass has no findings to leave unconfirmed. If its reset fails, the contract's `parallel-unconfirmed` "with the unconfirmed findings in parallel_only" fits poorly, and its discarded first pass leaves the cell with no driven result. (3) What `findings` holds on a `parallel-unconfirmed` or `sequential-reset` cell (empty, null, or the parallel findings) is not stated.
findings.implementation_impact: Different implementations give different states and exit codes for the same failure. Plan and aggregate consumers may read leftover `findings` on an inconclusive record as a fail signal, for example when picking a focus cell.
findings.suggestion: Add matrix rows covering: reset fails before engine 1's rerun while engine 2 also needs a pass; reset fails before a BO-login fallback pass. State that `findings` is `[]` on these child-set inconclusive cells, with the parallel findings only in `parallel_only`.

findings.location: Design Notes > `scenario_spans` vs Confirmation merge (BO-login fallback "replaces the cell's driven fields wholesale")
findings.issue: One note says `scenario_spans` (and `started_at`) always come from the first, lockstep pass. The other says the BO-login fallback replaces the driven fields wholesale. Spans, `started_at` and `bo_authed` are not explicitly in or out of "driven fields". The contract also discards the fallback engine's first-pass result.
findings.implementation_impact: If spans and started_at are replaced, the overlap acceptance criterion and live test (c) become false or vacuous for that cell, because the sequential pass trivially overlaps nothing. If they are kept, the record mixes a discarded pass's timing with another pass's results.
findings.suggestion: List the replaced fields explicitly for the fallback (findings, inconclusive, authored_assertions, bo_authed, console_errors, screenshots, finished_at, scenarios_run). State whether `started_at` and `scenario_spans` stay from the lockstep pass, and have live test (c) skip cells that used the fallback.

findings.location: Always > Child (lockstep barrier, "no timeout") / parallel driver
findings.issue: The barrier's liveness depends only on the version process creating `<engine>.done` when it reaps a worker. If the version process itself dies (crash, OOM, SIGKILL after the stop grace period), a surviving worker waits on `barrier-wait` forever, because no timeout is the stated rule. The spec also does not say what the version process does with live workers when its own code raises.
findings.implementation_impact: Orphaned worker processes stay registered under the Job ID, emit ALIVE lines forever, and keep the browser open. `--cleanup-orphans` treats the owner as alive.
findings.suggestion: Require workers to exit when the parent pid is gone (check `os.getppid()` or the parent pid's liveness in the barrier and lock poll loops). Require the version process to SIGTERM and reap workers in its `finally` before teardown. Add a unit test that kills the parent mid-barrier.

findings.location: Tasks > ps-e2e-run.py engine worker (`--engine-worker <spec.json>`, result file)
findings.issue: Neither the spec nor the contract defines the worker spec JSON (engine, scenarios, ctx, lock/step paths, result path, job id, progress file), the result file schema (cell fields plus phase entries in recorded order), or what "parseable" means. That includes a truncated write, or a result present with a non-zero exit. The worker also must not go through `fl.run_main_with_progress`, which always writes `DONE`; the spec only says "never `DONE`".
findings.implementation_impact: Crash detection is ambiguous, and "timings re-recorded in order so suffixes continue" cannot be implemented consistently without a schema. A worker stopped by SIGTERM through the usual wrapper writes `DONE rc=stopped` into the version's log, so the runner reads the version as finished.
findings.suggestion: Pin down the minimal schemas. The result file is written atomically (temp file plus `os.replace`). Parseable means a JSON object with the agreed keys, whatever the exit code. The worker entry bypasses `run_main_with_progress` (or passes a flag that suppresses DONE).

findings.location: I/O matrix row Parallel-only failure ("reset phases `#2` in `boot_phases`") / Always > Reset bullet ("`#n` suffixes")
findings.issue: `TimingSink.record` suffixes per name from the second occurrence. The first confirmation reset therefore records `reset-db`, `reset-files`, `reset-opcache` with no suffix, and only `wait-http#2` and `warmup-bo#2` get `#2`. The matrix (and the contract wording) implies `reset-db#2`.
findings.implementation_impact: Tests written to the matrix fail against the existing sink, or someone "fixes" the sink to force suffixes and breaks CAP-6 keys elsewhere.
findings.suggestion: State the exact expected keys for one and two confirmation passes, for example `reset-db`, `reset-files`, `reset-opcache`, `wait-http#2`, `warmup-bo#2`, then `reset-db#2` and so on.

findings.location: Acceptance Criteria #1 / I/O matrix row Parallel clean
findings.issue: "Both start before either ends" is satisfied by any implementation that spawns both workers before reaping either, even one that serializes every scenario. A take-`LOCK_EX`-always bug would pass. Nothing checks that FO-only scenarios actually overlap across engines, or that parallel mode saves time. On bankwire, 5 of 6 steps (the smoke plus four specs) are BO, so the lock serializes almost everything. Meanwhile any finding adds a full reset plus a full sequential rerun per failing engine, which can make a failing gate boot slower than the sequential fallback (where fail-fast skips firefox).
findings.implementation_impact: The Problem statement's speed-up promise goes unverified. A regression to full serialization would ship green, and the failure-path cost is not acknowledged.
findings.suggestion: Add a criterion (unit with real threads, and live) that FO-only steps' spans overlap across engines. Record the expected gain and the failure-path cost explicitly, at least as a note feeding the deferred bankwire timing report.

findings.location: Boundaries > Honesty law; Problem statement (shared state)
findings.issue: Confirmation reruns only findings. Within a lockstep step, engine B's BO scenario still runs after engine A's run of the same scenario has mutated the shop, and FO-only scenarios run concurrently against one DB. A failure that only shows on fresh state (first-time config save, empty table) can therefore be masked into a pass on the later engine. It is never rerun, so the claimed identity with one cold run per engine does not hold by construction.
findings.implementation_impact: False passes are possible in parallel mode, the one failure class the honesty law exists to prevent. The Identical findings live test uses a fault that fails on every engine, so it cannot detect masking.
findings.suggestion: Acknowledge the residual risk explicitly (or escalate as an Ask First contract change), and add a live fixture that only fails on fresh state to the identical-findings test. Or document that `{browser}`-unique data is required for spec authors and why that is sufficient.

findings.location: Always > Runner ("a version any of whose configured cells has a newest record with reason `parallel-unconfirmed` ... is always admitted at cost 1 sequential")
findings.issue: The forcing lasts only while `parallel-unconfirmed` is the newest record. In the forced sequential run, a `fail` on the first engine makes the second engine `not-run`, which becomes its newest record, so the next run goes parallel again and can repeat `parallel-unconfirmed` indefinitely. If the root cause is the reset routine itself, the forced sequential run needs the same reset and produces `sequential-reset`. The remedy then cannot help, and nothing says so.
findings.implementation_impact: An oscillation between parallel-unconfirmed, not-run and parallel-unconfirmed never reaches `blocked-infra` (`not-run` breaks the pair), so the operator gets neither evidence nor a clear block.
findings.suggestion: Base the forcing on the newest record that is not `not-run`/`no-slots`, or on any `parallel-unconfirmed` record in the current session. Add a matrix row for a persistent reset failure to show it ends in `blocked-infra`.

findings.location: Tasks > tests/live/test-cap7-live.py (b)/(c); Verification command 3
findings.issue: (b) and (c) run through `ps-run-layer.py --cells V:chromium+firefox` on a shared daemon. If fewer than 2 slots are free, admission silently falls back to cost 1 `--sequential-browsers`. (c) then checks sequential records, where no spans overlap anyway, so it passes vacuously, and (b) does not test parallel confirmation at all.
findings.implementation_impact: The CAP-7 live contract can be "proven" without parallel mode ever running.
findings.suggestion: Require the test to assert `browser_mode: parallel`, the presence of `rerun-seq:<engine>` phases, and overlapping `started_at`/`finished_at` on the records it checks. Fail (not skip) when admission fell back to sequential, or reserve slots via `--slots` and a pre-check of daemon usage.

findings.location: Verification (live command "expected: exit 0") / Acceptance Criteria #2
findings.issue: The live suite skips when Docker, either browser, or an image is missing, and a skip exits 0. The Verification and the acceptance criterion ("(a), (b) and (c) pass on every default target version") therefore cannot tell a pass from a skip. `PSM_LIVE_VERSIONS` can also narrow the versions without the criterion noticing.
findings.implementation_impact: The slice can be marked verified when no live check ran, or ran on one version only.
findings.suggestion: Have the suite print a machine-checkable summary (ran/skipped per test and version), and require the verification to show (a), (b) and (c) ran on every default target with `PSM_LIVE_VERSIONS` unset.

findings.location: Design Notes > Confirmation merge (`finished_at` from the counting pass, `started_at` from the first pass)
findings.issue: Confirmation passes run one after another in `psm_e2e_browsers` order. A later engine's `finished_at` therefore comes after the earlier engine's reset and rerun as well. The cell's `wall_clock` (`finished_at` minus `started_at`) counts another engine's reset and rerun time as its own.
findings.implementation_impact: CAP-6 per-cell wall-clock and the deferred bankwire timing report misattribute time: the second engine looks slow whenever the first engine had a finding.
findings.suggestion: Either document that a cell's wall_clock spans its first-pass start to its own pass's end, including queueing behind other engines' passes, or keep `finished_at` from the lockstep pass and rely on `rerun-seq:<engine>` for the rerun's duration.

findings.location: Always > Child ("Every scenario holds `fcntl.flock` ...; `_bo_login` runs outside it") / live test (a)
findings.issue: Engine B's `_bo_login` can run while engine A already holds `LOCK_EX` for step 0 (the universal smoke is BO), because the login happens before the first scenario and outside the lock. Live test (a) proves only the sequence "A logs in, B logs in, then each loads". It does not cover a login that overlaps another engine's running BO scenario (session or token churn mid-scenario on PS 8/9).
findings.implementation_impact: Intermittent BO findings or inconclusive steps on the first BO step. These are then confirmed away or produce BO-login fallbacks, which adds reruns and flakiness that the live suite does not exercise.
findings.suggestion: Either do every engine's `_bo_login` before barrier step 0 (all engines log in, then the first barrier), or extend live test (a) to log B in while A is mid-way through a BO page sequence.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap7-parallel-browsers.md:28 (Always, lock + lockstep)
findings.issue: Order of lock release vs barrier wait is unspecified: 'releases it before the engine's next scenario' permits holding the bo.lock while blocked in barrier-wait for step k+1.
findings.implementation_impact: Engine A holds LOCK_EX/LOCK_SH at the barrier while engine B blocks in lock-wait on the same file for step k; neither has a timeout, so the version deadlocks forever.
findings.suggestion: State explicitly: the scenario's flock is released (fd closed) as soon as the scenario ends and before the step-k marker is created / barrier-wait begins; add a unit test with two threads where a BO scenario is followed by a barrier.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap7-parallel-browsers.md:27 (Always, parallel driver reaping)
findings.issue: Reaping order of workers is unspecified; '.done' is created only 'when it reaps a worker'.
findings.implementation_impact: If the version process blocks on wait() for worker A while worker B has already crashed, B's '<engine>.done' is never created, A waits in barrier-wait forever (no timeout) and the 'barrier never hangs' row fails.
findings.suggestion: Require reaping in completion order (os.waitpid(-1)/poll loop over all workers) with '.done' created immediately on each exit; test with a stub worker that exits 1 at step 0 while the other is still at the barrier.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap7-parallel-browsers.md:27,58 (worker entry in main)
findings.issue: Worker entry is placed in main, but main is wrapped by fl.run_main_with_progress, which always writes a DONE line (rc, crash or stopped).
findings.implementation_impact: Workers write DONE into the version's progress log in the middle of the run, which breaks the 'never DONE' rule and makes watchers treat the version as finished early.
findings.suggestion: Specify that --engine-worker is dispatched before run_main_with_progress (e.g. in __main__) or that the wrapper skips DONE/progress_init in worker mode; add a test asserting no DONE line from a stub worker.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap7-parallel-browsers.md:27 (SIGTERM / --stop-job)
findings.issue: No behavior is given for a stop arriving during or before the sequential confirmation passes, or for a worker SIGTERMed directly by --stop-job before the version process.
findings.implementation_impact: A worker killed by --stop-job leaves no result and is recorded as 'crash' rather than stopped. The version process may also start a reset plus rerun after SIGTERM and overrun JOB_STOP_GRACE (SIGKILL), so no teardown runs.
findings.suggestion: Add rule: once SIGTERM is received (or any worker exits with -15/143), skip all confirmation/fallback passes and resets, go straight to teardown and exit 143; never classify a signal-terminated worker as crash.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap7-parallel-browsers.md:27 (one engine stays in-process)
findings.issue: Wording 'one engine stays in-process and sequential' is ambiguous: it can mean a single-engine version, or that one of the parallel engines runs in-process instead of in a worker.
findings.implementation_impact: An implementer may run one parallel engine in-process. That contradicts 'one --engine-worker subprocess per engine' and puts two sync Playwright instances in one process.
findings.suggestion: Reword: 'a version process driving exactly one probed engine drives it in-process with browser_mode: sequential; in parallel mode every engine runs in its own worker'.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap7-parallel-browsers.md:85 (Confirmation merge)
findings.issue: Merge rule does not say whether launch_error, browser_notes, scenarios_run and authored_assertions come from the first pass or the rerun when the rerun's in-process browser fails to launch or crashes after launch.
findings.implementation_impact: A rerun with launch_error yields empty findings, so every parallel finding moves to parallel_only. The cell can then read pass (first-pass launch_error null) or launch-error inconclusive, never parallel-unconfirmed, so an unconfirmed finding can pass silently.
findings.suggestion: Add: a rerun with launch_error or an exception after launch is unconfirmable, so the cell is inconclusive with reason parallel-unconfirmed, every parallel finding goes to parallel_only, and the launch error goes to cell errors and browser_notes.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap7-parallel-browsers.md:85 (Confirmation merge, inconclusive at same key)
findings.issue: A parallel finding whose (scenario, step, action) is inconclusive in the rerun (e.g. rerun BO login failed) is treated as 'not reproduced'.
findings.implementation_impact: F moves to parallel_only without being confirmed or refuted. The cell becomes pass with inconclusive steps instead of parallel-unconfirmed, so the next admission is not forced sequential and the plan sees inconclusive-steps.
findings.suggestion: Specify: a parallel finding whose key is inconclusive in the rerun counts as unconfirmed, so the cell is inconclusive with reason parallel-unconfirmed and F goes to parallel_only; add an I/O row.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap7-parallel-browsers.md:85 (bo_authed kept from first pass)
findings.issue: bo_authed stays from first pass even when the rerun's BO login failed and made BO steps inconclusive.
findings.implementation_impact: The record says bo_authed=true while the counting pass's BO steps are inconclusive for lack of auth. The record is self-contradictory and misleads infra diagnosis.
findings.suggestion: Define bo_authed as first-pass AND rerun login result (or add rerun_bo_authed), and note the rerun login failure in browser_notes.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap7-parallel-browsers.md:46 + cell-contract Parallel browsers (BO-login fallback + reset failure)
findings.issue: BO-login fallback engine whose pre-pass reset or health check fails (or snapshot failed) has no defined state or parallel_only content; its first pass was discarded.
findings.implementation_impact: The implementation must guess whether to keep the discarded first pass, emit parallel-unconfirmed with empty parallel_only, or emit sequential-reset. Records diverge from the contract's honesty law.
findings.suggestion: Add I/O row: fallback engine + reset/snapshot failure → inconclusive, parallel-unconfirmed, parallel_only = discarded first-pass findings (or []), failing sub-phase in cell errors.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap7-parallel-browsers.md:27,32 (sequential passes after a confirmed fail)
findings.issue: Unspecified whether later engines still get their reset + rerun after an earlier engine's rerun confirms a fail, and whether a reset failure for engine 1 stops attempts for engine 2.
findings.implementation_impact: The child may skip later reruns, which leaves their cells unconfirmed. It may also retry resets on a broken container, which wastes boot time. Either way the records are not reproducible across implementations.
findings.suggestion: State: in parallel confirmation every engine needing a pass gets one (no inner fail-fast); after the first reset/health failure every remaining engine needing a pass is parallel-unconfirmed with that sub-phase, no further reset attempted.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap7-parallel-browsers.md:84 vs cell-contract Runner > Fail-fast (sequential fallback)
findings.issue: Precedence is unspecified when the snapshot fails AND the first engine fails: the design note gives later engines sequential-reset, while fail-fast gives them not-run.
findings.implementation_impact: Later engines get sequential-reset (an infra cause that counts toward blocked-infra) or not-run, depending on code order. That changes plan derivation and admission.
findings.suggestion: Add rule: fail-fast wins, so after a first-engine fail the remaining engines are not-run even when the snapshot failed; sequential-reset applies only when the engine would otherwise have started.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap7-parallel-browsers.md:86 (reset-db)
findings.issue: The prelude's $MYSQL includes $DBN as the default database; after dropping it, loading the --databases dump through $MYSQL fails with 'Unknown database'.
findings.implementation_impact: Every reset-db fails. Every rerun becomes parallel-unconfirmed and every later sequential-fallback engine becomes sequential-reset, which breaks the core CAP-7 confirmation path.
findings.suggestion: Specify the loader connects without a default DB ("$MYSQL_BIN -h $DBH -P $DBPORT -u $DBU -p$DBPW < dump") and the dump invocation ("$MYSQLDUMP_BIN ... --single-transaction --routines --databases $DBN").

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap7-parallel-browsers.md:29,86 (snapshot storage location)
findings.issue: Where the dump and docroot list are stored (container path, host tmp) and their cleanup are unspecified.
findings.implementation_impact: If they are stored under the docroot after the listing, reset-files deletes them (comm -13) and the next reset (#3) cannot restore. If they are stored on the host, the in-container shell cannot read them.
findings.suggestion: Fix paths outside /var/www/html inside the PS container (e.g. /tmp/psm-cap7-snapshot.sql, /tmp/psm-cap7-docroot.lst), created before use and removed by teardown.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap7-parallel-browsers.md:86 (reset-opcache)
findings.issue: Picking the php-fpm master via /proc/*/comm is ambiguous, because master and pool workers share the same comm (php-fpm / php-fpmX.Y).
findings.implementation_impact: USR2 sent to workers (or to all php-fpm processes) does not reload opcache, or it kills in-flight workers. Stale opcache then serves the pre-reset module code to the rerun.
findings.suggestion: Define master selection: php-fpm process whose PPid is not a php-fpm process (or read pid from the fpm pid file); if more than one or none, fall back to apachectl, else fail.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap7-parallel-browsers.md:29,86 (wait-http / warmup-bo after reset)
findings.issue: Unspecified whether wait-http or warmup-bo failing after a reset counts as a 'reset phase failed'; today warmup-bo is best-effort and wait-http continues on 5xx-but-responded.
findings.implementation_impact: A rerun against a shop still returning 5xx after reset may produce confirmed findings that are reset artefacts, or the same condition may yield parallel-unconfirmed. Either outcome changes the gate.
findings.suggestion: Specify: after a reset, wait-http with no response → reset failure (parallel-unconfirmed / sequential-reset); 5xx-but-responded and warmup-bo outcome keep first-boot semantics (best-effort).

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap7-parallel-browsers.md:86 (health check before reset)
findings.issue: The health check is one-shot 'healthy'. _health_status also returns 'unknown' (docker timeout), 'starting' and 'nohealth', and no handling is given for these.
findings.implementation_impact: A transient docker CLI timeout turns a confirmable cell into parallel-unconfirmed and forces the next run sequential. The error text naming the sub-phase is also undefined.
findings.suggestion: Use wait_healthy with a bounded timeout (retry on unknown/starting), treat gone/unhealthy/timeout as failure, and name the sub-phase 'health' in cell errors.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap7-parallel-browsers.md:86 (reset-files, module source)
findings.issue: The fresh module copy comes from the live /ps-module-src bind mount, so a module patched on the host mid-run yields rerun code different from the parallel pass.
findings.implementation_impact: The rerun confirms or refutes findings against different code, so the parallel_only and findings split is meaningless for that run.
findings.suggestion: Snapshot the installed modules/$MOD_NAME tree in-container at snapshot-db time and restore from that copy, or record that the source fingerprint must be rechecked before the rerun.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap7-parallel-browsers.md:86 (reset-files, deleted files)
findings.issue: Docroot files present at the snapshot but deleted during a pass (outside modules/$MOD_NAME) are neither restored nor mentioned; only 'modified' files are called out.
findings.implementation_impact: A scenario that deletes core or theme files leaves the rerun with a damaged shop. Rerun failures then count as blocking confirmed findings.
findings.suggestion: Either detect missing snapshot paths (comm -23) and fail the reset (unconfirmed / sequential-reset), or document deletions alongside modifications as a known non-restored case.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap7-parallel-browsers.md:70 (TimingSink re-recording / browser phase ownership)
findings.issue: The spec does not say whether the worker or the version process records 'browser:<engine>' for the parallel pass. It also does not say whether rerun-seq:<engine> contains a nested browser:<engine>#2 and the reset phases.
findings.implementation_impact: If both processes record it, a spurious 'browser:<e>#2' appears, which is indistinguishable from the BO-login fallback pass. Rerun timings also differ depending on implementation.
findings.suggestion: State: only the worker records browser:<e> (re-recorded once); rerun-seq:<e> wraps reset + drive and emits no browser:<e>#n; the fallback pass emits browser:<e>#2 after its reset.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap7-parallel-browsers.md:74 + ps-e2e-run.py substitute/assemble_findings ({browser} = <engine>-seq)
findings.issue: Sequential passes set {browser} to '<engine>-seq'. Today {browser}, finding 'browser', message prefix and drive_engine's engine all read the same ctx['engine'] value.
findings.implementation_impact: Rerun findings may carry browser 'chromium-seq'. Identical-findings comparison on (version, browser, scenario, step, action) then fails, and getattr(p, 'chromium-seq') cannot launch.
findings.suggestion: Specify a separate substitution token value (ctx['browser_token']) for {browser}; the engine name in findings, inconclusive and launch stays '<engine>'.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap7-parallel-browsers.md:83 (scenario_spans keying)
findings.issue: scenario_spans is keyed by scenario name, but discover_scenarios does not dedupe names: two specs can share 'name', or an authored spec can be named like the universal smoke.
findings.implementation_impact: Spans overwrite each other, so the live overlap and lockstep tests (c) check incomplete data and can pass falsely.
findings.suggestion: Key spans by step index or source (e.g. '<k>:<source>'), or reject/notes duplicate names at discovery.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap7-parallel-browsers.md:27 (version-level legacy fields)
findings.issue: Version-level fields res['findings'], ['inconclusive'], ['pass'], ['browsers'], ['screenshots'] and result['pass'] in parallel mode are unspecified: first pass, confirmed result, or which pass's screenshots.
findings.implementation_impact: Direct runs (the quickstart TDD loop reads findings) show unconfirmed parallel findings or miss confirmed rerun findings, which diverges from the cells and the exit code.
findings.suggestion: State: version-level fields are rebuilt from the cells' confirmed results (findings = union of cell findings, pass = no cell fail, screenshots = counting passes).

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap7-parallel-browsers.md:27 (all workers crash / launch fail)
findings.issue: When every worker crashes or fails to launch, skipped_browser, res['browsers'] and whether confirmation passes run are unspecified.
findings.implementation_impact: The version may be reported as skipped_browser (a coverage gap), or as crash cells only. Both are inconsistent with the sequential path, where all-launch-failed sets skipped_browser.
findings.suggestion: Add I/O row: all workers crash → each cell crash, no sequential pass, skipped_browser false, exit 1; all launch_error → existing skipped_browser semantics.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap7-parallel-browsers.md:27 (direct runs in parallel, slot cost)
findings.issue: Direct runs go parallel by default but keep --slot-cost default 1, so the psm.slots label under-counts the browsers actually driven.
findings.implementation_impact: Concurrent ps-run-layer admissions count a two-browser direct run as one slot, which oversubscribes the daemon cap.
findings.suggestion: Specify that a direct parallel run stamps psm.slots = number of engines driven when --slot-cost is not given (or state that direct runs are knowingly exempt).

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap7-parallel-browsers.md:27-28 (lock file / step dir I/O errors and orphans)
findings.issue: Behavior on OSError when creating or opening <job>-<ver>.bo.lock or the .step dir is unspecified, as is who creates the step dir and cleanup after a SIGKILLed version process.
findings.implementation_impact: Workers may crash (cells become 'crash') or run without lock/barrier and silently mask cross-engine interference. Stale lock files and step dirs also accumulate in /tmp/psm-locks.
findings.suggestion: Version process creates the step dir (mode 1777 parent as slots.lock does) before spawning; on failure fall back to --sequential-browsers behaviour with a logged note; cleanup_orphans removes <job>-* of dead jobs.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap7-parallel-browsers.md:27 (worker hang)
findings.issue: There is no bound on a worker that hangs outside step timeouts (sync_playwright startup, browser.close, launch); lock-wait and barrier-wait are explicitly unbounded.
findings.implementation_impact: One hung worker stalls the other engine indefinitely and holds n slots forever. Only --stop-job recovers.
findings.suggestion: Add a per-worker wall-clock limit (e.g. scenarios x steps x nav_timeout + launch margin) after which the version process kills it and records crash with a note.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap7-parallel-browsers.md:31 (parallel-unconfirmed history read)
findings.issue: Admission forcing reads history 'once before admission', but there is no handling for an unreadable history file (OSError) or a history whose newest line is corrupt.
findings.implementation_impact: The runner crashes, or the forcing is silently skipped, so a version with an unconfirmed history is driven in parallel again.
findings.suggestion: Specify: history read error → input error (exit 2) or treat as forced sequential; corrupt-history cell → forced sequential.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap7-parallel-browsers.md:27 (worker result schema)
findings.issue: 'Parseable result' covers only JSON parse. A parseable result with missing or wrong-typed keys, or with a cell for a different engine, is unspecified.
findings.implementation_impact: A malformed result raises KeyError in the version process (crashing the whole version) or yields an incomplete cell that is later read as incomplete-record.
findings.suggestion: Validate the worker result shape (engine matches, required cell keys present); any mismatch → that cell crash with the exit code and reason in browser_notes.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap7-parallel-browsers.md:73 (live test image presence)
findings.issue: Behavior when only some default-tag images are present locally is unspecified (skip the whole suite or only those versions).
findings.implementation_impact: The live suite either skips entirely (and hides results for present versions) or fails on a missing image. The acceptance criterion 'pass on every default target version' then becomes unverifiable.
findings.suggestion: Specify: skip the whole suite with a message naming missing images, unless PSM_LIVE_VERSIONS narrows to versions whose images are all present.

findings.location: Boundaries > Always (bullet 2, 'Every pass records `scenario_spans`'); Tasks > ps-e2e-run.py ('`scenario_spans` in every pass'); Design Notes > `scenario_spans` and > Confirmation merge
findings.issue: These contradict each other. Boundaries and Tasks say every pass records `scenario_spans`. Design Notes say spans come only from the cell's first pass (the lockstep pass) and that 'sequential passes are timed only by their phases'. The merge note then says the BO-login fallback's second pass 'replaces the cell's driven fields wholesale' but never says whether `scenario_spans` is one of those fields. Live test (c) reads spans from (b)'s parallel records, so the answer decides what (c) can check.
findings.implementation_impact: The implementer has to guess whether the rerun-seq pass, the BO-login fallback pass and the sequential-fallback engines emit spans, and whether a fallback record keeps the lockstep spans, takes the second pass's spans or gets null. Unit tests and live test (c) will assert different things depending on the guess.
findings.suggestion: State one rule per pass type. For example: lockstep worker pass and every sequential-fallback engine emit spans; rerun-seq and BO-login fallback passes do not, and the record keeps the lockstep spans. Then remove 'Every pass records' or correct it, and list `scenario_spans` explicitly as kept or replaced in the BO-fallback merge.

findings.location: I/O matrix row 'Parallel-only failure' ('reset phases `#2` in boot_phases'); Boundaries bullet 3 ('`#n` suffixes'); cell-contract Parallel-only failures ('suffixed `#2`, `#3`')
findings.issue: `TimingSink.record` (ps-flashlight-run.py:464) leaves the first occurrence of a name unsuffixed and gives repeats `#2`, `#3`. The first reset in a boot is the first `reset-db`/`reset-files`/`reset-opcache`, so the sink records it as `reset-db`, not `reset-db#2`. Only `wait-http#2`/`warmup-bo#2` get the suffix naturally. The spec (and contract) expect `#2` on the reset phases of the first sequential pass.
findings.implementation_impact: The I/O row is untestable as written unless the implementer special-cases reset names (numbering by pass) or changes TimingSink semantics, and either choice may also break CAP-5's later reuse of the routine (a warm iteration's first reset has no suffix).
findings.suggestion: Decide whether the reset phases follow TimingSink (first reset `reset-db`, second `reset-db#2`) or are numbered by pass (first pass = `#1` implicit, sequential passes `#2`, `#3`). Rewrite the I/O row with the exact expected `boot_phases` keys for a one-rerun and a two-rerun case.

findings.location: Boundaries/Tasks/Design Notes on `rerun-seq:<engine>`; Tasks > docs (SKILL.md lists both `rerun-seq:` and `browser:<e>#2`); I/O 'BO-login fallback'
findings.issue: The spec never says what `rerun-seq:<engine>` wraps. It could cover the reset phases plus the drive, or only the drive, and the rerun may or may not also open a `browser:<engine>#2` phase. Contract Phase timings gives `browser:<engine>#2` only for the BO-login fallback. Separately, the rerun sets `{browser}` to `<engine>-seq`. If the drive code builds its phase name from the token (as today, where `{browser}` = `ctx['engine']`), it records `browser:chromium-seq`, which lands in `phase_durations['chromium-seq']` and is dropped.
findings.implementation_impact: The implementer has to guess the nesting and naming. That changes which keys appear in `phase_durations`, whether `derive_state`'s `_driven` check (`browser:<engine>` or `browser:<engine>#n`) sees the counting pass, and what the docs tell operators to watch.
findings.suggestion: Specify the phase tree for each sequential pass. For example: rerun = `rerun-seq:<engine>` around [reset-db, reset-files, reset-opcache, wait-http, warmup-bo, drive], with no extra `browser:` phase; BO fallback = reset phases then `browser:<engine>#2`. Also state that the phase name always uses the engine name, never the `{browser}` token value.

findings.location: Tasks > ps-e2e-run.py ('`--engine-worker <spec.json>`, parsed before the normal argparse', 'worker timings re-recorded into the version sink in order'); Boundaries bullet 1 ('reads each worker's result file')
findings.issue: The spec.json schema, the result-file path and format, and the shape of the worker timing data are all undefined. Re-recording 'in order so suffixes continue' cannot use `TimingSink.as_dict()`, whose keys are already suffixed, so the worker must emit an ordered list of (base name, seconds, outcome) entries. The spec also doesn't say how the pre-parse avoids catching the existing `--engines` flag or argparse prefix abbreviations of it.
findings.implementation_impact: This is the worker/version-process interface. Two engineers (or the unit-test stub worker) would invent incompatible formats. Getting the timing shape wrong breaks the `#n` continuity the spec requires.
findings.suggestion: Add a short schema: spec.json fields (version, engine, scenarios, ctx minus page handles, job_id, run_id, progress_file, lock path, step dir, result path, screenshot dir, headed, nav_timeout, engine order) and result JSON (engine result as `drive_engine` returns it, plus `timings: [[name, seconds, outcome], ...]` in record order, plus `scenario_spans`). Require an exact `argv[1] == '--engine-worker'` match.

findings.location: Boundaries bullet 1 (worker 'lines appended to the version's progress log, never `DONE`') vs cell-contract Parallel browsers bullet 1
findings.issue: Two load-bearing claims from the contract are missing. First, 'Only the version process calls `progress_init`'. Second, worker lines are 'tagged `browser:<engine>`'. That matters here because `fl.phase` and `fl.progress` write only once `_PROGRESS['path']` is set, and only `progress_init` sets it. `fl.run_main_with_progress` also always writes `DONE`.
findings.implementation_impact: A worker that calls `progress_init(..., truncate=False)` breaks the contract. One that doesn't call it writes nothing, so `lock-wait`/`barrier-wait` heartbeats vanish. If the worker reuses `run_main_with_progress`, it writes `DONE`. Line tagging is unspecified either way.
findings.suggestion: State the mechanism. For example, add a flashlight helper that points `_PROGRESS` at an existing log without truncating (or write through `progress_to`). Name the tag form (the phase field `browser:<engine>`, or a detail prefix). Say that the worker entry bypasses `run_main_with_progress`.

findings.location: Tasks > ps-e2e-run.py ('cross-engine lock + holder markers'); Boundaries bullet 2 ('`lock-wait:<engine>` naming the holders')
findings.issue: 'Holder markers' appear only in Tasks and are never defined: no location, no file format, no create/delete order relative to `flock`, no stale-marker handling after a crash. `flock` itself cannot name its holders. The cleanup rule lists only the lock file and the step dir.
findings.implementation_impact: The implementer has to invent a marker scheme. The ALIVE detail and the unit tests ('lock and barrier with real flock/files across threads') can't be written against a fixed expectation, and leftover markers in `<tmp>/psm-locks` aren't covered by cleanup.
findings.suggestion: Define the markers, e.g. `<LOCK_DIR>/<job>-<ver>.bo.holders/<engine>` created after the flock is acquired and removed before release. A crashed worker's marker is ignored once `<engine>.done` exists. The version process deletes the holders dir with the lock file and step dir.

findings.location: Boundaries bullet 2 (lock and barrier waits); cell-contract Phase timings ('`lock-wait:<engine>` and `barrier-wait:<engine>` per scenario that waits')
findings.issue: Several mechanics are left open. The spec doesn't say whether `lock-wait`/`barrier-wait` open only when a non-blocking attempt fails (the contract says 'per scenario that waits'; the spec omits this), what the poll interval is, or whether the barrier index k is 0- or 1-based. It also doesn't say whether k counts the universal smoke, or when (relative to `_bo_login`) the first barrier and lock apply.
findings.implementation_impact: Unit tests that count `lock-wait:<engine>#n` entries, and the live test (c) step ordering, depend on these choices. An always-open wait phase would add an entry for every scenario.
findings.suggestion: Carry over 'opened only when the first non-blocking try fails'. Name a poll constant (e.g. 0.5 s, patchable in tests). Fix k as the 0-based index into the discovery-ordered list including the smoke at 0. Say that `_bo_login` runs before step 0 with no lock and no barrier.

findings.location: Design Notes > 'Snapshot failure in the sequential fallback' vs cell-contract Parallel browsers > Slots and Boundaries > Ask First
findings.issue: The contract says that when the snapshot or a reset fails, 'every engine not yet driven gets `state: inconclusive`, reason `sequential-reset`'. A snapshot failure happens right after `warmup-bo`, before any engine has run, so every engine is 'not yet driven', the first included. The spec's 'the first engine still runs' changes that contract rule, which Ask First reserves for the human. The spec also doesn't say which wins when the snapshot failed and the first engine then fails: fail-fast `not-run` or `sequential-reset`.
findings.implementation_impact: The implementer can't follow both the contract and the spec, and has no rule for the not-run vs sequential-reset precedence. The resulting records differ (`not-run` is not an infra cause; `sequential-reset` is, and feeds `blocked-infra`).
findings.suggestion: Either get the contract amended (the first engine may run because it needs no reset) or follow the contract (every engine `sequential-reset`). Add an I/O row: snapshot fails + chromium `fail` → firefox reason = ? (suggest `not-run`, since fail-fast comes first and no reset is attempted).

findings.location: Boundaries bullet 1 ('at most one sequential pass per contract before teardown'); Design Notes > Snapshot failure; I/O 'Unconfirmable'
findings.issue: The spec doesn't cover what happens when a reset fails partway through parallel confirmation. If chromium's reset fails, does firefox still attempt its own reset and pass, or does it become `parallel-unconfirmed` without trying? The state of a BO-login-fallback engine is also unspecified when its reset fails or the container is unhealthy. Its first pass is discarded and it may have no findings, so `parallel-unconfirmed` with an empty `parallel_only` is possible, as is keeping the discarded pass or another inconclusive reason. For the unhealthy-container case, the 'sub-phase in cell errors' has no phase name to record.
findings.implementation_impact: There are several plausible implementations with different records and exit codes. Tests for the 'Unconfirmable' row can't pin down what the other engine does.
findings.suggestion: Add rules and I/O rows for: (1) a failed reset for engine A → engines later in order skip their reset and become `parallel-unconfirmed`, or still try (pick one); (2) a BO-fallback engine whose reset fails → state, reason, and what `parallel_only` holds; (3) the `errors` text when health ≠ healthy (e.g. `health: <status>`).

findings.location: cell-contract Parallel browsers bullet 3 ('When every engine's login fails, or the second login fails too, ... with no further rerun') vs Boundaries 'Honesty law' (a parallel finding blocks only when the sequential rerun reproduces it)
findings.issue: The spec doesn't settle whether 'no further rerun' stops `rerun-seq` confirmation for an engine whose BO login failed in the parallel pass but which has (FO) findings. If it does, those parallel findings would block unconfirmed, which breaks the honesty law the spec restates. If it doesn't, the contract wording is misleading. Neither the spec nor the I/O matrix covers 'all logins fail + findings'.
findings.implementation_impact: The implementer has to pick. One choice lets an unconfirmed parallel finding block. The other contradicts the contract text.
findings.suggestion: Add an I/O row: both logins fail, chromium has FO finding F → `rerun-seq:chromium` still runs (no BO-fallback pass), and F counts only if reproduced. Reword 'no further rerun' as 'no further BO-login fallback pass'.

findings.location: Boundaries 'Honesty law'; Design Notes > Confirmation merge; I/O 'Unconfirmable'
findings.issue: The rerun itself can degrade, and the spec doesn't say how. Cases: (a) the engine fails to launch in the rerun (`launch_error`); (b) BO login fails in the rerun, so BO finding F becomes an inconclusive step, moves to `parallel_only`, and the cell ends `pass` with inconclusive steps; (c) `wait-http` gets no response, or `warmup-bo` fails, after the reset. The 'unconfirmable' rule covers only snapshot, reset phases and container health.
findings.implementation_impact: In case (b) a blocking parallel finding turns into a non-blocking `pass` while `bo_authed` (kept from the first pass) still reads true. Cases (a) and (c) may come out as `launch-error`/`errors` instead of `parallel-unconfirmed`. Any of these could break the identical-findings guarantee without anyone noticing.
findings.suggestion: Classify each case explicitly. Suggested: a rerun with `launch_error`, a failed BO login while a parallel BO finding is pending, or `wait-http` with no response → `parallel-unconfirmed` with the parallel findings in `parallel_only` and the failing sub-phase in cell `errors`.

findings.location: Design Notes > Confirmation merge (field list) and BO-login fallback ('replaces the cell's driven fields wholesale'); `_run_one_version_inner` version-level fields
findings.issue: The merge list leaves out `scenarios_run`, `browser_notes` (rerun notes), `launch_error` and `phase_durations`, including whether the discarded fallback first pass keeps its `browser:<e>`/`lock-wait` entries. 'Driven fields' is never defined. Keeping `bo_authed` and `authored_assertions` from the first pass can contradict the rerun's inconclusive BO steps. The legacy version-level output (`findings`, `inconclusive`, `pass`, `browsers`, `screenshots`, `console_errors`, `authored_assertions`), which direct runs print and `overall_pass` uses, is built today from the in-process `driven` list. The spec doesn't say whether it reflects confirmed or parallel results.
findings.implementation_impact: The implementer has to make a merge decision for each field, and those decisions show up in history records and in direct-run JSON (the quickstart TDD loop reads `findings`/`pass`). Tests can't be written against an expected record.
findings.suggestion: Give the full per-field merge table for rerun-seq and for the BO fallback (define 'driven fields' as the `_fill_cell` keys plus `started_at`/`finished_at`/`scenario_spans`). State that the version-level legacy fields are rebuilt from the final (confirmed) cells.

findings.location: Boundaries bullet 1 ('direct runs included'); SPEC Constraints ('E2E concurrency (... plus CAP-7 browsers) respects one configurable host-wide cap'); cell-contract Config keys (`--slot-cost` '1 when absent, e.g. a direct ps-e2e-run.py run')
findings.issue: After this change a direct two-engine `ps-e2e-run.py` run drives both browsers in parallel, but it stamps `psm.slots=1` because `--slot-cost` defaults to 1. The daemon-wide cap then undercounts CAP-7 browsers, which contradicts the SPEC constraint. The spec doesn't address the direct-run cost at all.
findings.implementation_impact: The implementer has to choose between following the contract default (undercounting parallel direct runs) and stamping n (departing from the contract text). The CAP-3 'Labels' test (no `--slot-cost` → 1) may then need changing.
findings.suggestion: Decide explicitly. Either a direct parallel run without `--slot-cost` stamps n (contract amendment, update the Labels test), or record a deliberate exception ('direct runs bypass admission and count 1, as documented') and update the docs to say so.

findings.location: I/O row 'Parallel clean' ('spans overlap, `browser:<e>` phases overlap')
findings.issue: The universal smoke has a BO step and takes the lock exclusively, so its spans can never overlap across engines. 'Spans overlap' can hold only for FO-only scenarios, and the row doesn't say which. `phase_durations` entries are just `{seconds, outcome}` with no timestamps, so a record can't show that `browser:<e>` phases overlap.
findings.implementation_impact: A literal test would either fail (smoke spans) or be unwritable (phase overlap from records). The implementer has to guess what to assert.
findings.suggestion: Rewrite: 'FO-only scenarios' spans overlap across engines; BO scenarios' spans don't; cells' `started_at`/`finished_at` overlap (the stand-in for the browser phase overlap); progress-log START/END of both `browser:<e>` lines interleave'.

findings.location: Acceptance Criteria 1 ('a two-engine version admitted at cost 2 ... boots once and its two cells' started_at/finished_at overlap'); Tasks > tests ('child rows with a stubbed parallel driver')
findings.issue: The spec doesn't say which test proves AC 1. With a stubbed parallel driver the overlap comes from the stub itself, so the check proves nothing. Only 'the worker spawn path once with a real stub worker subprocess' or the live suite exercise real concurrency. 'Boots once' has no observable either: one `bring-up` in `boot_phases`, one `boot_id` across both records, or one container label.
findings.implementation_impact: AC 1 could be 'met' by a tautological test, and reviewers can't check it reproducibly.
findings.suggestion: Tie AC 1 to a named test: ps-run-layer with a real child and stub worker subprocess (or the live suite), asserting both records share `boot_id`, `boot_phases` holds exactly one `bring-up`, both have `browser_mode: parallel`, and max(started_at) < min(finished_at).

findings.location: Tasks > tests ('the worker spawn path once with a real stub worker subprocess')
findings.issue: The spec gives no seam for swapping in a stub worker. The real worker is `sys.executable ps-e2e-run.py --engine-worker ...`, which imports Playwright and launches browsers. There's no env var, spec.json field or module constant for redirecting the spawn command or stubbing `drive_engine` inside a separate process.
findings.implementation_impact: The implementer has to add an undocumented test hook, or the test drives real Playwright, which unit tests can't do since they run without Playwright or Docker.
findings.suggestion: Name the seam, e.g. a module-level `WORKER_CMD` (list) patched by tests to run a tiny stub script that writes a canned result file and creates step files. Alternatively, a spec.json `stub_result` field honoured only when an env var like `PSM_E2E_TEST_STUB_WORKER=1` is set.

findings.location: Tasks > tests/live/test-cap7-live.py; Acceptance Criteria 2; Verification command 3 ('expected: exit 0')
findings.issue: Several live-test points are open. (1) A skipped run (Docker, browsers or images absent) presumably exits 0, which looks identical to a pass, so 'exit 0' can't prove that (a)–(c) passed. (2) The test isn't required to assert `browser_mode: parallel` and `--slot-cost 2`. On the shared daemon, missing free slots make ps-run-layer admit at cost 1 sequentially, so (b)/(c) would silently test the sequential fallback, or (c) would fail with spans that aren't lockstep. (3) It's unspecified how (a) boots a container per version: through ps-e2e-run internals, or a special spec. (4) The test needs a PEP723 header with `playwright` to drive the sessions in (a) itself. (5) (b) needs `--session` (`--new-session`), `--tier`, a `--config` (require_config rejects a missing one when psm-config.json exists) and a temp reports dir, none of which are specified. (6) The scope of the 'mismatch reruns once' retry (parallel run only, or the baselines too) isn't defined.
findings.implementation_impact: The live suite can pass while testing nothing, or fail for environmental reasons. The implementer has to invent the harness.
findings.suggestion: Require: skip = a distinct exit code or a printed 'SKIPPED' that the verification command checks; assert `browser_mode == 'parallel'` on both (b) records, and treat a sequential admission as 'retry or fail with a message'. Specify the (a) boot path, the PEP723 deps, the config/session/tier/reports-dir setup for (b), and that the mismatch retry reruns the whole (parallel + both baselines) triple once.

findings.location: Design Notes > Reset in shell ('`reset-db` = drop the DB with the prelude creds, then load the `--databases` dump'); Boundaries bullet 3 (`DB_PRELUDE`)
findings.issue: `DB_PRELUDE` (ps-scenario-run.py:80) defines `$MYSQL` and `$MYSQLDUMP` with `$DBN` already appended as a positional database. After `DROP DATABASE`, loading with `$MYSQL < dump` connects to the now-missing `$DBN` and fails with 'Unknown database'. The spec also doesn't say where the dump and the docroot list live. They must sit outside `/var/www/html` (or `reset-files` sees them) and must not collide with Layer 5's `/tmp/psm-scenario-baseline.sql`.
findings.implementation_impact: A literal implementation of 'drop then load with the prelude creds' fails at every reset, so every confirmation ends `parallel-unconfirmed`. Paths have to be guessed.
findings.suggestion: Specify the commands: dump `$MYSQLDUMP_BIN -h $DBH -P $DBPORT -u $DBU -p$DBPW --databases $DBN > /tmp/psm-e2e-snapshot.sql`, load with `$MYSQL_BIN` without a default DB, docroot list at `/tmp/psm-e2e-snapshot.files`. State that the user from `parameters.php` must be able to DROP/CREATE that database.

findings.location: Boundaries bullet 3 ('`DB_PRELUDE` (lazily `load_sibling`ed)'); Code Map ('ps-scenario-run.py -- `DB_PRELUDE`, `load_sibling` (reused, unchanged)')
findings.issue: The spec doesn't say which `load_sibling` to use. ps-scenario-run.py's own `load_sibling` can't load ps-scenario-run.py itself. ps-e2e-run.py has no `load_sibling`, only `_plan_layers()`. ps-aggregate.py has one. Loading ps-scenario-run.py also runs its top-level `fl = load_sibling(ps-flashlight-run.py)`, which creates a second ps-flashlight-run instance with its own `_PROGRESS`, `_TIMING`, `_JOB` and `RUN_ID`, and its `load_sibling` calls `sys.exit(2)` on failure.
findings.implementation_impact: An implementer may call the wrong loader or accidentally use the second `fl` instance's `_exec`/`phase`. Its timing sink and progress state are inactive, so phases recorded through it are lost. A load failure in the middle of a run would exit 2 from inside the version process.
findings.suggestion: Say: load ps-scenario-run.py with a local loader in ps-e2e-run (the `_plan_layers` pattern), read only `DB_PRELUDE` from it, and always use ps-e2e-run's own `fl` for `_exec`/`phase`. A load failure counts as a `snapshot-db` failure, not an exit.

findings.location: Design Notes > Reset in shell ('`reset-opcache` = `kill -USR2` the php-fpm master found via `/proc/*/comm`')
findings.issue: On the nginx flashlight images the php-fpm master and its pool workers have the same comm (`php-fpm`, or a version-suffixed name truncated to 15 characters). `/proc/*/comm` alone can't identify the master. That needs the ppid (from `/proc/<pid>/stat`) or the cmdline `php-fpm: master process`.
findings.implementation_impact: If USR2 goes to every matching pid, or to the first one, the opcache reload may miss the master or signal workers in unpredictable ways. The tests and the CAP-5 reuse depend on getting this right.
findings.suggestion: Specify the selection: pids whose comm starts with `php-fpm` and whose parent's comm does not (or whose cmdline contains `master process`). Exactly one must match, otherwise the step fails. Add a unit test over a fake /proc listing.

findings.location: Boundaries bullet 3 (reset routine); Design Notes > Mode; Evidence record fields `boot`/`boot_id`
findings.issue: The spec never says that records produced after a reset (a rerun-seq counting pass, or a sequential-fallback later engine) keep `boot: cold` and the version's `boot_id`. Gate-grade requires `boot: cold`. Because the routine is 'written so CAP-5 can reuse it', and CAP-5 warm iterations use `boot: warm` and a composite `<keeper boot_id>#<RUN_ID>`, an implementer could mark reset passes as warm or give them a new `boot_id`.
findings.implementation_impact: That would make every confirmed or fallback cell non-gate-grade, or count the boot twice in `e2e_phase_durations`.
findings.suggestion: Add: 'reset passes stay within the same cold boot — `boot: cold`, unchanged `boot_id`, one `boot_phases` object holding the reset phases.'

findings.location: Boundaries bullet 5 (Runner: '`parallel-unconfirmed` (read once before admission)'); Code Map ps-plan-layers `read_history`
findings.issue: The spec doesn't say what happens if the history read fails. `read_history` raises `PlanInputError` on OS errors, so it's unclear whether that means exit 2, or a warning plus parallel admission. It also doesn't say how 'newest record' is defined when the file has a corrupt tail, or whether the cells checked are all configured cells of the version or only the admitted ones. For n == 1 it's unclear whether `--sequential-browsers` is still passed when forced. The spec's wording ('a version driving n engines ... else at cost 1 with `--sequential-browsers` when n > 1') leaves both n == 1 cases unstated.
findings.implementation_impact: Each of these is a guess that changes the child argv and test expectations, e.g. the 'Unconfirmed history' row on a corrupt file.
findings.suggestion: Pin down: an unreadable history → InputError exit 2 before spawn (consistent with other pre-spawn checks); 'newest' = last valid record whatever the corrupt tail; all configured browsers of the version are checked; n == 1 → cost 1 without `--sequential-browsers`.

findings.location: Boundaries bullet 1 ('one engine stays in-process and `sequential`')
findings.issue: The wording is ambiguous. It can be read as 'in parallel mode one of the engines runs in-process and the others in workers', which contradicts 'spawns one `--engine-worker` subprocess per engine'. The intended reading is probably 'a version process driving one engine runs it in-process with `browser_mode: sequential`'.
findings.implementation_impact: One reading leads to the wrong architecture (n-1 workers).
findings.suggestion: Rephrase: 'A version process driving a single probed engine, or started with `--sequential-browsers`, drives in-process with `browser_mode: sequential`.'

findings.location: cell-contract Slots ('... drives its browsers one after another ... and logs the fallback') and Parallel browsers bullet 3 ('The fallback is logged'); existing ps-e2e-run.py `main` stderr message
findings.issue: The existing stderr message for `--sequential-browsers` still reads '(admisi interim cost 1)' and the CAP-3 comment says 'BUKAN kekurangan slot'. Under CAP-7 the sequential mode means slot shortage or `parallel-unconfirmed` forcing, so the message is wrong. The spec doesn't mention updating it, and doesn't say where the BO-login fallback is logged. It needs to go somewhere other than `browser_notes`/`errors`, since `browser_notes` would drop `ready`.
findings.implementation_impact: Stale or misleading operator messages ship. The implementer may log the BO-fallback in `browser_notes` and silently make the cell non-passing.
findings.suggestion: Specify both log lines: the sequential-fallback reason (slots or unconfirmed history, ideally passed by ps-run-layer or just 'sequential mode') on stderr and the progress log; the BO-login fallback on stderr and the progress log only, never in `browser_notes`/`errors`.

findings.location: Tasks > docs (SKILL.md, run-phases.md, e2e-quickstart.md, README)
findings.issue: Several existing passages are left stale. SKILL.md line 47 ('sampai CAP-4/5/7 selalu dingin & skenario penuh') and run-phases.md line ~136 ('Interim sampai CAP-4/5/7 ... browser berurutan sesuai admisi slot') still describe sequential browsers. e2e-quickstart.md 'DB bersama antar-browser' (line ~207) and the screenshot path example `.../9.1/chromium-<scenario>-*.png` (line ~152) are now wrong. The visual-review instruction 'tinjau `<run dir>/<ver>/`' (SKILL.md line 47, run-phases.md line ~198) doesn't cover the `<ver>/<engine>/` and `<ver>/<engine>-seq/` folders, or which pass's images count. README has no 'E2E concurrency' section, so where the slot-cost text goes is a guess.
findings.implementation_impact: Operators get docs that contradict the new behaviour. They may review the discarded first-pass screenshots instead of the counting pass.
findings.suggestion: Add these passages to the docs task: replace 'CAP-4/5/7' with 'CAP-4/5' in both interim notes; rewrite the quickstart shared-DB gotcha (lockstep + reset; `{browser}` still needed for same-step data) and the path example; tell visual review to use the record's `screenshots` (counting pass). For README, point the text at the `psm_e2e_slots` table row and the `--slots` mentions (lines ~59/86/91/357).

findings.location: Boundaries bullet 1 (screenshots in `<shots>/<ver>/<engine>`); Design Notes / contract ('`<shots>/<ver>/<engine>-seq`' for sequential passes)
findings.issue: The screenshot directory is specified for workers and for sequential passes only. It's unspecified for the sequential fallback's engines and for a single-engine version, whether they stay in `<shots>/<ver>/` as today or move to `<shots>/<ver>/<engine>/`. The spec also doesn't say whether the discarded BO-fallback first pass's images are kept or deleted.
findings.implementation_impact: The layout varies by mode in ways that tests and the docs can't predict, and stale first-pass PNGs may sit next to the counting ones.
findings.suggestion: Choose one layout for every mode (suggested: always `<shots>/<ver>/<engine>[-seq]/`) and say that discarded-pass images stay on disk but are absent from the record's `screenshots`.

findings.location: Boundaries bullet 1 ('forwards SIGTERM'; 'A worker that leaves no parseable result → ... `crash`'); Never ('producing `stopped` records')
findings.issue: Workers are registered under the Job ID, so `--stop-job` sends SIGTERM to them directly as well as to the version process. The spec doesn't say what the version process emits when a worker exits 143 or is killed. A worker killed by its own signal (e.g. OOM, or someone signalling its pid) would become `crash` with rc in `browser_notes`. But when the version process is itself stopped, it should exit 143 with no output. The ordering and race between the two cases is unspecified.
findings.implementation_impact: There's a risk of emitting `crash` cells (an infra cause feeding `blocked-infra`) for an operator stop, or of hanging while waiting for already-signalled workers.
findings.suggestion: State: once the version process has received SIGTERM, it forwards it, reaps workers with a bound (e.g. `JOB_STOP_GRACE`), tears down and exits 143 without emitting cells. A worker rc of 143/-15 while the version process was not signalled → `crash` with rc noted.

findings.location: Design Notes > `scenario_spans` ('`{<scenario name>: [start_ns, end_ns]}`'); Boundaries bullet 2 (lockstep)
findings.issue: Spans are keyed by scenario name, but today `discover_scenarios` doesn't reject duplicate effective names (that check is CAP-4's `requires` validation, which is deferred). Two specs with the same `name` would overwrite each other's span, and lockstep step identity by name would be ambiguous.
findings.implementation_impact: Live test (c) and the lock-overlap checks could pass or fail spuriously for modules with duplicate names. The implementer has to choose between keying by index and keying by name.
findings.suggestion: Either key spans by step index (with the name inside) or state that duplicate names are not handled until CAP-4 and that the barrier uses the step index k, never the name.
